discovery_articles.title: Murales del Borgo San Giuliano in Rimini, Italy
discovery_articles.snippet: Founded around the year 1000, Borgo San Giuliano, was originally the city's fishermen’s quarter. The tradition of painting murals that has made Borgo San Giuliano famous has deep roots. In 1979, the city council suggested demolishing the neighborhood to make way for a new residential development.

discovery_articles.title: Fannie Bay Gaol in Fannie Bay, Australia
discovery_articles.snippet: For nearly a century, Fannie Bay Gaol was the Northern Territory of Australia's principal prison, confining a range of prisoners from cattle rustlers and opium traffickers to political prisoners and condemned murderers. It was opened as Her Majesty's Gaol and Labour Prison in 1883 and remained in use until 1979. This made it one of Australia's longest operating frontier prisons.

discovery_articles.title: The Atlas Obscura Guide to the World's Strangest Christmas Traditions
discovery_articles.snippet: Every European Christmas market sells the same mulled wine out of the same wooden hut. This is not a criticism — it is a very good hut, and the wine is warm. But it is not a reason to choose one country over another, and the "best Christmas markets" lists that dominate December travel writing are, functionally, lists of interchangeable huts.

fern_data.greeting: What does a morning actually ask of you — to slow down, or to go somewhere entirely?
